cards.text: Some visitors come to Jesus: Pharisees and scribes, religious leaders and teachers of the law, who came all the way from Jerusalem. They've got a question for Jesus about His disciples. Friend, when somebody comes in from out of town and opens with a question about your crew, it is NOT a compliment question.

cards.question: The Pharisees and scribes say Jesus' disciples break the tradition of the elders. What are the disciples doing?

answers.text: They don't wash their hands before they eat
They don't fast twice a week like others
They don't pray three times every day

cards.question: The Pharisees and scribes asked about the disciples eating with unwashed hands. Jesus answers with a question of His own. What does He ask them?

answers.text: Why they break God's command for their tradition
Why they came all this way to ask about hands
Why they never wash their own hands either

cards.question: The first command of God that Jesus points to is the command to honor your father and mother. True or false?

cards.text: God also said, 'Anyone who curses his father or mother must be put to death.' But Jesus tells the Pharisees and scribes that what they say goes another way.

cards.question: In the Pharisees' teaching, a man tells his parents that whatever they would have received from him is a gift devoted to God. Their teaching says he still has to honor his parents with it. True or false?

cards.text: Jesus sums it up: the Pharisees and scribes nullify the word of God for the sake of their tradition. They came to talk about hands, and now THEY'RE the ones getting looked at.
Then Jesus says to them, 'You hypocrites!' He says Isaiah, one of Israel's prophets, prophesied correctly about them.

cards.question: In the words from Isaiah that Jesus quotes, these people honor God with their lips. Where are their hearts?

cards.text: Then the words go on: 'They worship Me in vain…' Big words, far-off heart: that's signing the office birthday card 'Love you SO much!' for a guy whose name you had to read off the envelope.

cards.question: In the words from Isaiah that Jesus quotes, these people teach the rules of ___ as doctrine.

cards.text: Then Jesus calls the crowd to Him and says, 'Listen and understand.' Friend, that's TWO jobs, and on a good day I'm good for one.

cards.question: Jesus tells the crowd what really defiles a man. What does He say defiles him?

answers.text: What comes out of his mouth

cards.text: Then the disciples come to Jesus with news about the Pharisees, who heard all that. It's that hallway huddle after a big meeting: 'So… did You notice?'

cards.question: The disciples tell Jesus how the Pharisees took His teaching about what defiles a man. How did the Pharisees take it?

cards.text: Jesus answers with a picture: 'Every plant that My heavenly Father has not planted will be pulled up by its roots.' Not trimmed, not moved to a new pot, but pulled up by its ROOTS.
Then Jesus tells the disciples what to do about the Pharisees: 'Disregard them! They are blind guides.' Short, plain, and no follow-up meeting on the calendar.

cards.question: Jesus says if a blind man leads a blind man, both of them will fall into a pit. True or false?

cards.text: Then Peter, one of Jesus' disciples, says, 'Explain this parable to us.' Peter, my friend, I am RIGHT there with you.

cards.question: Peter asks Jesus to explain the parable. Before explaining, Jesus asks the disciples a question. What does He ask?

answers.text: Why they told Him about the Pharisees
If the crowd had understood it

cards.question: Jesus explains the first half of the parable. According to Jesus, where does whatever enters the mouth go?

answers.text: Into the stomach and then out
Into the blood and stays there
Into the mind and changes it

cards.question: Jesus says the things that come out of the mouth come from the ___, and these things defile a man.
Jesus names what comes out of the heart. Which of these is on His list?
Jesus brings it back to where the Pharisees and scribes started. He says eating with unwashed hands defiles a man. True or false?
